ent_standard_iso_13849.name: ISO 13849
ent_standard_iso_13849.summary: A safety standard for the design of control systems on machinery, specifying performance levels (PL) and safety categories for risk reduction.
ent_standard_iso_13849.body:
## Overview

ISO 13849 is a functional safety standard for safety-related parts of control systems (SRP/CS) in machinery, published by the International Organization for Standardization. It quantifies the ability of safety functions to still execute correctly under fault conditions using PL (Performance Level) ratings a–e. What it truly changes is not the abstract promise of "how safe the robot is," but the concrete method of "how to prove safety using auditable engineering parameters." Humanoid robots operating in human-robot collaborative environments must have their safety-related control systems meet functional safety requirements: when a fault occurs, the system must still be able to bring the robot into a safe state [37][38].

ent_standard_iec_61508.name: IEC 61508
ent_standard_iec_61508.summary: An international standard for functional safety of electrical/electronic/programmable electronic safety-related systems, foundational for industrial and robot safety.
ent_standard_iec_61508.body:
## Overview

IEC 61508 is the fundamental functional safety standard for electrical/electronic/programmable electronic safety-related systems published by the International Electrotechnical Commission. It defines Safety Integrity Levels (SIL) from SIL1 to SIL4, quantifying the ability of a safety function to correctly execute under fault conditions using the probability of dangerous failure. What it truly changes is not "how to make systems more reliable," but rather a fundamental shift in safety philosophy: "when the system fails, how do we ensure it still enters a safe state?"

ent_standard_iso_13482_personal_care_rob.name: ISO 13482 Personal Care Robot Safety
ent_standard_iso_13482_personal_care_rob.summary: Safety requirements for personal care robots including service humanoids.
ent_standard_iso_13482_personal_care_rob.body:
## Overview

ISO 13482 Personal Care Robot Safety is an international standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in 2014, addressing safety requirements for personal care robots (including service humanoid robots). What it truly changes is not "what robots can do," but "the manner in which robots are permitted to exist alongside humans"—by establishing verifiable safety boundaries for human-robot coexistence through systematic risk assessment and inherent safety design.

ent_standard_iso_ts_15066_2016.name: ISO/TS 15066 Collaborative Robots Safety
ent_standard_iso_ts_15066_2016.summary: Technical specification defining safety requirements for collaborative robot systems, including force and pressure limits for human-robot contact.
ent_standard_iso_ts_15066_2016.body:
## Overview
ISO/TS 15066 is a technical specification published by the International Organization for Standardization, providing the first quantitative framework for safety requirements of collaborative robot systems in human-robot collaborative operations, particularly defining force and pressure limits for various body parts during contact. It fills the gap in industrial robot safety standards (such as ISO 10218) for "human-robot shared space" scenarios, shifting safety assessment from "avoiding contact" to "controlling the consequences of contact."

ent_standard_ul_fcc_ce.name: Regional Market Certifications (UL / FCC / CE)
ent_standard_ul_fcc_ce.summary: The set of mandatory or voluntary certifications required to sell robots in specific regions, such as UL for North America, CE for Europe, and FCC for electromagnetic compatibility.
ent_standard_ul_fcc_ce.body:
## Overview

Regional market certification is a combination of mandatory or de facto technical thresholds that humanoid robots must meet before entering the market of a specific country or region. It covers the EU CE marking, US UL certification and FCC certification, China CCC certification and CR robot certification, Japan PSE and Radio Law certification, among others. What it truly changes is not the testing process of a single product, but rather the elevation of safety, electromagnetic compatibility, and functional safety from "remedial items" after design to first-class inputs of the system architecture.

ent_paper_hartmann_evolution_of_safety_r.name_en: Evolution of Safety Requirements in Industrial Robotics: Comparative Analysis of ISO 10218-1/2 (2011 vs. 2025) and Integration of ISO/TS 15066
ent_paper_hartmann_evolution_of_safety_r.summary: This paper compares ISO 10218-1/2:2011 with their 2025 revisions and analyzes the normative integration of ISO/TS 15066, highlighting expanded functional safety, cybersecurity, software validation, and new robot classification requirements.
ent_paper_hartmann_evolution_of_safety_r.body:
## Overview
Industrial robotics has established itself as an integral component of large-scale manufacturing enterprises. Simultaneously, collaborative robotics is gaining prominence, introducing novel paradigms of human-machine interaction. These advancements have necessitated a comprehensive revision of safety standards, specifically incorporating requirements for cybersecurity and protection against unauthorized access in networked robotic systems. This article presents a comparative analysis of the ISO 10218:2011 and ISO 10218:2025 standards, examining the evolution of their structure, terminology, technical requirements, and annexes. ent_concept_product_liability.name: Product Liability
ent_concept_product_liability.summary: The legal responsibility of manufacturers and sellers for injuries or damages caused by defective or unsafe products, directly applicable to humanoid robots.
ent_concept_product_liability.body:
## Overview

Product liability refers to the legal responsibility of manufacturers and sellers for personal injury or property damage caused by defective or unsafe products, and it directly applies to humanoid robots. Traditional product liability law distinguishes among manufacturing defects, design defects, and warning defects, but the learning-based behavior and continuous evolution characteristics of humanoid robots pose a systematic challenge to this framework. What truly changes is not the rule of "who pays," but the underlying logic of "when, by whom, and with what evidence a defect is defined."

ent_concept_privacy_biometrics.name: Privacy and Biometrics
ent_concept_privacy_biometrics.summary: The governance of personal data and biometric information collected by robots, including face recognition, voiceprints, and gait data.
ent_concept_privacy_biometrics.body:
## Overview

Privacy and Biometrics refers to the rules, technologies, and architectural systems for governing the personal information and biometric data (face, voiceprint, gait, etc.) continuously collected by humanoid robots as mobile sensor platforms. What it truly changes is not "how data is collected," but "how privacy protection becomes an architecture-level decision rather than a post-hoc patch, under the premise that the data flywheel operates legally."
